key_insight: A closed-form harmonic model predicts oscillating-foil forces and power from motion inputs, linking higher harmonics to discrete vortex-shedding events.
engineering_relevance: The model offers a fast alternative to high-fidelity simulations for renewable-energy foil design and array optimization.
method: Decompose lift and pitching moment into odd Fourier harmonics.
Regress harmonic coefficients on 16 physics-based polynomial terms using two Ridge steps.
Reconstruct instantaneous forces and power from prescribed foil kinematics.
evidence_signal: Across 405 two-dimensional simulations, the model achieved leave-one-out R² = 0.98 for cycle-averaged power, 9% median peak error for instantaneous lift, and median phase error below 1% of the period.
watch_item: Validation is limited to the simulated two-dimensional kinematic parameter space; three-dimensional performance and extrapolation remain unestablished.
paper_title: Harmonic structure and parametric prediction of instantaneous power in oscillating foils
